text:
emma.docs: Quick note — I'm opening a micro-PR to standardize our function/tool-calling + structured-output docs. Plan: canonical invoice + user_intent schemas, add a compact schema_ref example, and a short "consumer test" snippet for CI. Will open in ~20m.

tariq.eng: 👍 please include a compact envelope example for mobile clients that points to /docs/schemas via schema_ref. I can run the parser harness to validate outputs.

emma.docs: Draft plan:
- Add /docs/schemas/invoice.json and /docs/schemas/user_intent.json
- Show full-envelope + compact "schema_ref" envelope
- Guardrails: validate -> partial-parse -> fallback-to-text
- Small CI check snippet to run in docs CI

ivy.devex: I'll update the TS + Python SDK snippets to use the new structured_output param. Example compact envelope I'll add:
`{"tool_call":{"name":"fetch_invoice","arguments":{"id":"INV-900"}},"structured_output":{"schema_ref":"/docs/schemas/invoice.json"}}`

chris-qa: Note: runtime collapses single-item arrays unless `minItems:1` and trims trailing zeros on floats. I'll run the harness and paste observed outputs so examples match reality. Also suggest a one-line reviewer command: `make docs-lint && ./tools/parse_check --schema docs/schemas/invoice.json --prompts examples/invoice_prompts.txt`.

emma.docs: Good call — I'll add an "observed vs expected" bullet in the PR for any diffs. Also adding a short "gotchas" note about nullable arrays and `oneOf` ambiguity.

tariq.eng: Can we also keep a tiny low-bandwidth example that inlines just the minimal schema (id + amount) so readers see both approaches? I'll add that in a follow-up commit.

emma.docs: Sounds great. docs-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4999 by emma.docs

ivy.devex: Assigning @tariq.eng and @chris-qa as reviewers. Target merge: Fri EOD if CI passes.

emma.docs: Thanks team — will push first commit shortly and ping when it's up.
